# The packaging tool and everything it drags in, pinned by hash (#241).
#
# `package.yaml` builds the archive an operator installs. A version pin fixes
# which release is asked for and not which bytes arrive, so a republished
# release of any of the packages below could write what it liked into that
# archive. `pip install --require-hashes` refuses that, and pip refuses a
# partial set, which is why the whole transitive closure is here rather than
# the one package the job names.
#
# Regenerate with, from a clean directory:
#
#     pip download --only-binary=:all: --platform manylinux_2_17_x86_64 \
#         --python-version 3.12 --implementation cp --abi cp312 \
#         --dest wheels "jprm==1.1.0"
#     pip hash wheels/*
#
# The platform, interpreter and ABI arguments are the runner's, not the
# machine the file was generated on, and they are why the PyYAML line below
# names one wheel rather than the several that version publishes. `package.yaml`
# installs the interpreter with `actions/setup-python` and pins it to 3.12 for
# the same reason: a runner that moved to another minor version would want a
# wheel with a different ABI tag and no hash here would match it. That failure
# is loud, which is the point.
#
# A version moves here only together with a regenerated hash. A hash that does
# not match reds the packaging job rather than degrading quietly, and the job
# proves that it does on every run.

jprm==1.1.0 \
    --hash=sha256:a1d0ff899fe4425170624fe54189f41e14e2520fb068a04ea0fe47b85ce5338e

click==8.4.2 \
    --hash=sha256:e6f9f66136c816745b9d65817da91d61d957fb16e02e4dcd0552553c5a197b76
click-log==0.4.0 \
    --hash=sha256:a43e394b528d52112af599f2fc9e4b7cf3c15f94e53581f74fa6867e68c91756
python-slugify==8.0.4 \
    --hash=sha256:276540b79961052b66b7d116620b36518847f52d5fd9e3a70164fc8c50faa6b8
pyyaml==6.0.3 \
    --hash=sha256:ba1cc08a7ccde2d2ec775841541641e4548226580ab850948cbfda66a1befcdc
tabulate==0.9.0 \
    --hash=sha256:024ca478df22e9340661486f85298cff5f6dcdba14f3813e8830015b9ed1948f
text-unidecode==1.3 \
    --hash=sha256:1311f10e8b895935241623731c2ba64f4c455287888b18189350b67134a822e8

# Click asks for this one on Windows only. The marker is carried rather than
# the line dropped, because pip resolves the closure before it evaluates a
# marker and a closure missing an entry is a closure this file cannot claim to
# name. On the runner the marker is false and nothing is fetched.
colorama==0.4.6 ; platform_system == "Windows" \
    --hash=sha256:4f1d9991f5acc0ca119f9d443620b77f9d6b33703e51011c16baf57afb285fc6
